Subject: Unexpected post-renewal consumption — ask for one-time adjustment

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for a smooth renewal last month. Since the contract renewal (effective 2027-02-15) our platform telemetry shows an additional ~270k inference minutes (roughly 1.9M extra tokens) consumed in the last two weeks that weren’t in our committed buckets. We hadn’t anticipated this spike and it will push us materially over our monthly target.

We attached our internal usage export (usage_report_2027Q1.csv). Can Redwood help us with a one-time adjudication / credit so we can normalize billing for Feb? Ideally we’d either (a) receive a one-time invoice credit against the March invoice or (b) amortize a smaller adjustment over two cycles.

We’re open to Redwood’s recommended approach — want to avoid surprises in our CFO’s review. Appreciate a quick read and an indicative figure.

Best,
Rebecca Lin
Head of Product
Octave Health

Attachment: usage_report_2027Q1.csv (CSV, 42KB)

Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal consumption — ask for one-time adjustment

Rebecca —

Thanks for the data and for surfacing this quickly. I pulled the usage and ran a preliminary calc — looks like the extra consumption is primarily short-lived burst traffic tied to an integration test that ramped following the Feb 10 push. Two recommended paths:

- One-time credit: Redwood can apply a one-time credit equal to the overage at our standard overage rate (estimated $9,450). This would appear on the March invoice as a one-off credit line.
- Amortize: Alternatively, we can split that credit across March and April invoices (two equal credits of ~$4,725) if you prefer cashflow smoothing for your accounting team.

To proceed I need: (1) confirmation of preferred remediation (one-time vs amortize), (2) which invoice to target (March invoice # will be generated 2027-03-05), and (3) if you want any minor goodwill reduction from Redwood for the disruption — we can consider a small additional credit but would need approval from Finance.

I’m looping in Ben from Billing to confirm the mechanics.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
